title: Reserve a claimed cell's declared files at claim time, matching the release the cap already performs
action: Make bee cells claim (and claim-next) reserve the cell's declared files under the claiming --worker identity for that cell id, the same (agent, cell) key finish_cap_and_release already releases by. A reservation conflict refuses the claim, typed and zero-mutation, rolling back any partial reservations. A cell with no files claims exactly as today. Then correct packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md so the sentence matches shipped behavior.

truths: Claiming a cell that declares files creates reservations for exactly those paths under the --worker identity; bee reservations list shows them.
Capping that cell releases exactly those reservations through the EXISTING release path, with no edit to finish_cap_and_release or release_reservations_for_agent.
A claim whose declared files conflict with another agent's active hold is refused, names the holder, and leaves both the claim store and the reservation store byte-untouched.
A cell declaring files [] claims exactly as it does today, with no new refusal.
Re-claiming a cell the same agent already holds does not error on its own prior reservations.
claim-next takes the same path, so the cross-session door never hands out an unreserved cell.
packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md line 37 describes what actually happens after this change.
Every claim that succeeds today with no overlapping hold still succeeds with byte-identical output.

acceptance: Claim reserves the declared files under the worker identity and the cap's existing release frees them; a conflicting claim is refused zero-mutation naming the holder; an empty files list is unchanged; the worker-cell prompt matches shipped behavior; the cells:: suite is green.

trace.outcome: cells claim and claim-next now reserve the claimed cell's declared files under the claiming worker, matching the release the cap already performs; a conflict refuses typed and rolls the store back
deviations: reserve_path_atomic hardcodes session: None, so the claim calls the same shared pair one layer down (reserve_prechecks + reserve_exec) to thread its --session-id; without it every claim in concurrent mode would refuse with reserve's own SESSION_REQUIRED

rollback releases by (worker, cell), the only scoping the shared release door offers: if this call created a lease AND the worker also held an older lease for the same cell, the older one goes too. Recorded in the function doc; nothing is released when this call created nothing

checks.name: claim-reserves-declared-files
checks.evidence: Orchestrator ran the binary built from this cell's source against throwaway cell probe-a (files: [packages/probeA.rs]). After claim, bee reservations list showed 'wk-pa | cell probe-a | packages/probeA.rs' plus its cross_worktree mirror. Before this cell, the same sequence left the store empty.

checks.name: conflict-refuses-zero-mutation
checks.evidence: Claiming probe-b on the same path under wk-pb returned 'claim: RESERVATION_CONFLICT — ... nothing claimed; the claim was rolled back and the store restored as found: - wk-pa holds packages/probeA.rs (cell probe-a)'. probe-b remained status=open with trace.worker=None, and the reservation listing was unchanged.

checks.name: empty-files-list-unchanged
checks.evidence: probe-c declared files: [] and claimed normally; the reservation count stayed at 1 (probe-a's), so no new refusal and no spurious reservation.

checks.name: cap-releases-through-the-existing-path
checks.evidence: Capping probe-a printed 'Released 1 reservation(s): packages/probeA.rs.' and bee reservations list then printed 'No reservations.' The release path was not edited by this cell.

checks.name: release-half-untouched
checks.evidence: The cell's files list does not include handlers_close.rs; finish_cap_and_release and release_reservations_for_agent carry no diff.

checks.name: single-reserve-door-preserved
checks.evidence: reserve_path_atomic hardcodes session: None and would refuse with SESSION_REQUIRED whenever another session is live, so the claim calls the same pair one layer down (reserve_prechecks + reserve_exec) with its own --session-id. Recorded as a deviation; no second reservation path was written.
